title: spec review: S3c memory feeds skills and strategy: recurring procedural memory becomes learned-skill candidates, promoted skills are referenced from memory, workflow strategy outcomes live as structured WARM records with a Planner query (P30, P31)
spec:
orchestrator/skill_learning.py: add candidates_from_memory(root) using memory_store.search over kinds gotcha and decision: group records by shared components (at least 3 records over at least 2 distinct dates) whose bodies contain procedural language (imperative verbs such as run, check, set, use, never, always, before, after) and produce learned-skill proposals through the existing proposal path (same shape and quarantine/testing lifecycle as today's learned skills; provenance memory with the record ids). When a proposal's skill is promoted to active, memory_store.add records a tag skill:<skill_id> on each source record and memory_hot renders such records as one line pointing at the skill instead of the full body. orchestrator/strategy.py: at merge time (new hook: daemon.py joins the scope; in the merge path that marks a task merged, call strategy.record_outcome(task, root) which computes the token, usd, duration and fix-round figures the way strategy.observations() does today and writes the record) write one memory_store record kind strategy per merged execute task: title '<task_class> <band> <strategy name>', tags task_class:<x>, band:<b>, strategy:<name>, outcome first_pass|fix_rounds:<n>, body with tokens, duration, executor, fix rounds; source_task and source_goal set. CLI `orchestrator memory strategies [--task-class x] [--band b] [--json]` aggregates strategy records: per strategy name the count, first-pass rate, median tokens and duration, so the Planner asks what worked for this kind of task without reading retrospectives. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/17-memory-skills-strategy.md.
Spec review T-1182 folded in: (1) The merge-time hook is new (daemon.py never called strategy.py): implement strategy.record_outcome(task, root) reusing the computation of strategy.observations(), called from the daemon's merge path (scope adds orchestrator/daemon.py and tests/test_daemon.py). (2) Tagging source records with skill:<skill_id> lives inside skills_registry.transition() when the new state is active (scope adds orchestrator/skills_registry.py), so both `skills promote` and the generic `skills transition` paths tag. (3) Proposals from memory get roles = the union of the role fields of the source records' source tasks (looked up on the bus when present) with 'execute' as the default, never an empty list; a test asserts a proposal is selectable for execute. (4) Record shape for strategy records: Record.outcome holds first_pass or fix_rounds:<n>; tags carry only task_class:<x>, band:<b>, strategy:<name>; `memory strategies` aggregates on those fields.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Task worktrees carry no .orchestrator runs, tasks or decision_log state: tests use synthetic fixtures; for any measured numbers in docs run read-only against /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/.orchestrator via an explicit root argument. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Contracts of the earlier modules: .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and docs/hermes-hardening/*.md on this branch; read the merged modules before building on them.

risks.issue: daemon.py already binds the module-level name `root` to `failures.root` (`from .failures import (root, lineage, ...)` at line 14), a function used inside report_merge itself (`lineage_root = root(current)`). The spec's literal instruction to call `strategy.record_outcome(task, root)` from the merge path collides with this existing name: written as specified, `root` resolves to the `failures.root` function object, not a filesystem path, breaking the call (TypeError) or silently misrouting memory writes.

skill_learning.py, strategy.py, and skills_registry.py all default `root=STATE` and treat `root` as the `.orchestrator` directory itself (e.g. skill_learning._tasks does `Path(root)/"tasks"`). memory_store.py and memory_hot.py default `root=ROOT` and treat `root` as the repo root, computing `Path(root)/".orchestrator"/"memory"/...`. Confirmed by the existing test harnesses: tests/test_strategy.py and tests/test_skill_learning.py build `self.root = tmp/.orchestrator`, while tests/test_memory_store.py builds `root = tmp` (parent of `.orchestrator`). New calls from candidates_from_memory, record_outcome, and skills_registry.transition into memory_store must translate root (e.g. `Path(root).parent`) or every memory_store.search/add/get silently resolves to a bogus double-nested `.orchestrator/.orchestrator/memory` path that the CLI (which passes root=ROOT) never reads.

`roots` in observations() only includes execute tasks without `constraints.fix_round_for`. report_merge(task_id, r) can be invoked with a fix-round descendant task_id; in that branch it walks the ancestor chain and marks the lineage root merged via direct bus.update calls, never re-entering report_merge for the root. If the new merge hook calls strategy.record_outcome with the raw merged task_id instead of resolving to the lineage root first (mirroring strategy._root_id/attribution.lineage), no observations() row will ever match a fix-round task id and the strategy record is silently never written for that lineage.

add() derives the record id via `_record_id(kind, date, title)` when the caller leaves id blank, and is an upsert keyed by that id (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE). The spec's strategy record title is '<task_class> <band> <strategy name>' with no task id. Two different tasks merged the same day with the same task_class/band/strategy — an expected case for the aggregation the CLI is meant to compute — hash to the same id and silently overwrite each other, undercounting `memory strategies` and violating 'one record per merged execute task.' The spec must require the task id inside the record id (e.g. Record(id=f'strategy-{task_id}', ...)).

skill_learning.py has no `bus` import and its own `_tasks(root)` helper already reads task JSON directly from `root/tasks/*.json` rather than through orchestrator.bus, because bus.get() operates against the live production STATE/ROOT rather than an arbitrary `root` argument (the same reason memory_store._goal_from_bus and memory_hot._tasks guard bus calls by comparing root to ROOT). The spec's phrase 'looked up on the bus when present' for the roles-union lookup risks an unconditional bus.get(task_id) call that silently misses under the test harness's synthetic ORCH_ROOT, masking the very behavior the 'selectable for execute' test needs to verify.

propose() refuses any pattern with confidence < .6, but procedural-language groupings mined from gotcha/decision records have no natural success/failure outcome the way task patterns do (support/successes are computed from task acceptance elsewhere). The spec doesn't define how candidates_from_memory should compute confidence/evidence_strength for memory-sourced patterns, leaving the propose() gate threshold to an arbitrary implementer choice.

suggested_spec_changes: State explicitly how the STATE-style root used by skill_learning.py/strategy.py/skills_registry.py must be translated before any memory_store call (e.g. 'pass Path(root).parent to memory_store from these three modules'), and require a unit test that exercises this against tests/_harness.py's ORCH_ROOT layout.

Rename the daemon.py hook call site away from the ambiguous `root` argument (`strategy.record_outcome(task, STATE.parent)` or similar) and flag the collision with the existing `from .failures import root` binding so the executor doesn't shadow it.

Require record_outcome to resolve the merged task to its lineage root (same walk as strategy._root_id) before matching/writing a strategy row, and require the daemon to call it once per lineage root even when the merge event fires on a fix-round descendant.

Require the strategy record's id (not just title) to embed the task id, e.g. Record(id=f'strategy-{task_id}', kind='strategy', title=..., ...), to prevent upsert collisions between distinct tasks sharing task_class/band/strategy/date.
Specify that the roles-union lookup for memory-derived proposals reuses skill_learning._tasks(root) (or an equivalent root-aware file read) rather than calling bus.get() directly.
Define how candidates_from_memory computes confidence/evidence_strength for memory-sourced patterns so propose()'s 0.6 gate behaves deterministically.
